subject: general
question: Who had called for Direct Action Day?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Muhammad Ali Jinnah**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Muhammad Ali Jinnah** declared **‘Direct Action Day'** on **16th August 1946** and called for Muslims all over the country to suspend all businesses.
 
• Also known as the **1946 Calcutta Killings**, was a day of nationwide communal riots that led to large-scale violence between Muslims and Hindus in the city of Calcutta in the Bengal province of British India.
 
• The day marked the start of **The Week of the Long Knives**, now known as the ‘**Direct Action Day**’ ,16 August poised itself right next to perhaps one of the most important days in Indian history.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Jayaprakash Narayan**, popularly referred to as JP or Lok Nayak, was an Indian independence activist, theorist, socialist and political leader.
 
• **Subhash Chandra Bose** was an Indian nationalist whose defiance of British authority in India made him a hero among Indians, but his wartime alliances with Nazi Germany and Imperial Japan left a legacy vexed by authoritarianism, anti-Semitism, and military failure.
 
• **Mohandas Karamchand Gandhi **was an Indian lawyer, anti-colonial nationalist, and political ethicist who employed nonviolent resistance to lead the successful campaign for India's independence from British rule and to later inspire movements for civil rights and freedom across the world.
